claims.text: Dependabot version updates are configured by a .github/dependabot.yml file in the repository (version: 2, an updates list with package-ecosystem, directory or directories, schedule.interval); Dependabot opens pull requests when newer versions of the dependencies it watches exist.
claims.source_hint: GitHub docs: Dependabot > Configuring Dependabot version updates; Dependabot options reference (version, updates, package-ecosystem, directory, directories, schedule)

claims.text: Dependabot creates its pull requests from branches whose names start with dependabot/ (default prefix 'dependabot', separator '/').
claims.source_hint: GitHub docs: Dependabot options reference > pull-request-branch-name (separator, prefix); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 ci.yml:7

claims.text: A Dependabot update changes the pin itself: package version where declared plus the lock file (don-hang PR #8 regenerated packages.lock.json under CPM), and the commit SHA of an action pinned by SHA (PRs #1-#7). Docker digest updates are no longer claimed.
claims.source_hint: Execution evidence: don-hang Dependabot PRs #1-#8 (DECISIONS.md §3 2026-10-06 E1 and 2026-10-07); GitHub docs: Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

claims.text: Workflows triggered by pull_request run on pull requests opened by Dependabot, so ci.yml runs on each Dependabot pull request.
claims.source_hint: GitHub docs: Automating Dependabot with GitHub Actions (pull_request events from Dependabot trigger workflows, with restricted token)

claims.text: groups with update-types [minor, patch] puts matching updates of that ecosystem entry into one pull request; an update that matches no group (here a major update) is raised in its own individual pull request.
claims.source_hint: GitHub docs: Dependabot options reference > groups (update-types); Optimizing PR creation > grouping (ungrouped updates get individual PRs)

claims.text: Semantic versioning increments MAJOR for backward-incompatible changes to the public API; MINOR and PATCH are backward compatible.

cooldown (default-days) makes Dependabot wait until a release has been published for that many days before opening a version update pull request for it; cooldown applies to version updates only, not security updates.
claims.source_hint: GitHub docs: Dependabot options reference > cooldown (default-days)

claims.text: If a malicious release is found and removed from where it is published within the cooldown, no version-update pull request proposes it; the cooldown helps only if it is found within those days and only for updates that go through Dependabot.

dependabot.yml @ stage-3 lines 8-28: version 2; nuget at directory / and pub at /DonHang.App, each weekly, cooldown default-days 7, a group nuget-/pub-minor-and-patch with update-types [minor, patch].

dependabot.yml @ stage-3 lines 30-53: github-actions at / and docker with directories /DonHang.Api, /DonHang.Notifications, /DonHang.Payments, /fake-gateway, /lab, same weekly/cooldown/group settings; 4 package-ecosystem lines, 4 'default-days: 7' lines.

ci.yml @ stage-3 lines 1-9: on push with branches-ignore ['dependabot/**'], pull_request, workflow_dispatch (lets a person start the workflow by hand); nothing else in ci.yml treats Dependabot branches or pull requests differently.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 .github/workflows/ci.yml (whole file); GitHub docs: Events that trigger workflows > workflow_dispatch

claims.text: Dependabot runs on GitHub (as a GitHub service against the repository), so it cannot be run in Đơn Hàng's lab; STAGE.md at stage-3 states Dependabot runs only on GitHub.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 STAGE.md ("Dependabot runs only on GitHub, not in the lab"); GitHub docs: About Dependabot version updates

claims.text: Dependabot version updates propose newer releases regardless of known vulnerabilities; Dependabot security updates (PRs for vulnerable dependencies) are a separate feature enabled in the repository settings.
claims.source_hint: GitHub docs: About Dependabot version updates; About Dependabot security updates; Configuring Dependabot security updates (enable in Settings > Code security)

claims.text: A release published by whoever controls the package or action can be malicious if that control is taken over; a green CI run proves only that the release builds and passes the tests, not that it does nothing else.

Without a lock file, pub resolution with a ^ constraint picks the newest release allowed by the constraint, so the result can change without a commit (lesson ties this to pub, not NuGet, which prefers the lowest applicable version); pins make each update a reviewed, revertable commit.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: Dependency management (flutter pub upgrade / resolution within pubspec.yaml constraints); .NET docs: library-guidance/dependencies (NuGet lowest applicable version)

claims.text: Choosing the cooldown length is a trade-off: longer gives more time for a bad release to be found, and delays every fix; 7 days is Đơn Hàng's choice, not a required value.
claims.source_hint: depth_notes (no general recommendation for cooldown days); dependabot.yml comment lines 1-7
